tools.name: check_eligibility
tools.description: Check whether File US Taxes can prepare a federal return. Pass a two-letter US state code of the person's residence, or abroad=true for a US citizen living abroad. Returns eligible true or false. Does not take or return tax or identity data.

tools.name: get_prices
tools.description: Return the fixed USD prices for federal return preparation, with early and regular rates, the no-meeting and 30-minute-meeting options, and the early-rate end date. Same data as fileustaxes.com/services.json and /pricing/.

tools.name: start_signup
tools.description: Record a sign-up request for the 2027 season and return the portal sign-up link (client sign-ups are open). Only call after the person has typed their own name and email and said yes; set consent to true only then. Do not put tax documents, Social Security numbers or account numbers in any field. Id

tools.name: ask_tiny
tools.description: Answer a general question about File US Taxes from the approved FAQ library only (no generated answers). Returns matching FAQ answers with a link to the FAQ and to the Tiny chat page, or a fallback when nothing matches. Do not send personal or tax details.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start_signup · Private data: check_eligibility, start_signup, ask_tiny · Public sink: start_signup, ask_tiny.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start_signup · Private data: check_eligibility, start_signup, ask_tiny · Public sink: start_signup, ask_tiny

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
